problem: Multimodal representation learning using InfoNCE-based objectives creates inherent conflicts between alignment and uniformity across modalities, causing distribution gaps that worsen with more modalities.
approach: The paper proposes a principled decoupling of alignment and uniformity objectives for multimodal learning, enabling a conflict-free recipe that supports both discriminative and generative use cases by reformulating the learning problem geometrically.
contribution: Demonstrates that the proposed method acts as an efficient proxy for a global Hölder divergence over multiple modality distributions, reducing distribution gaps, with consistent gains on retrieval and generation tasks.

problem: Bayesian optimization for high-dimensional constrained problems suffers from the curse of dimensionality and trust-region methods prone to premature shrinking under tight or complex constraints.
approach: LCBO leverages differentiable constraint-penalized surrogates to alternate between rapid local descent and uncertainty-driven exploration, with theoretical guarantees on KKT residual convergence that scale polynomially with dimension.
contribution: Achieves polynomial convergence rates on the KKT residual for high-dimensional problems (up to 100D) and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

problem: Large Multimodal Models designed for offline settings are ill-suited for streaming video, with resource demands growing at least linearly with video duration, creating scalability bottlenecks.
approach: FlowNar introduces dynamic context management for historical visual context removal and CLAM (Cross Linear Attentive Memory) for streaming visual history retention, ensuring bounded memory and computational complexity.
contribution: Substantially improves narration quality over baselines while supporting 10× longer videos and achieving 3× higher throughput on Ego4D, EgoExo4D, and EpicKitchens100.

problem: Flow-based gradual domain adaptation relies on sample-based log-likelihood estimation which discards useful information and degrades performance when intermediate domains must be synthesized.
approach: Proposes Entropy-regularized Semi-dual Unbalanced Optimal Transport (E-SUOT) that reformulates flow-based GDA as a Lagrangian dual problem with entropy regularization, converting unstable min-max training into stable sequential optimization.
contribution: Provides theoretical analysis of stability and generalization, with extensive experiments demonstrating the efficacy of the E-SUOT framework for constructing intermediate domains.

problem: Long-horizon dialogue agents suffer from latent state drift where observable behavior, internal representations, and memory can diverge silently, creating asymmetric rupture risk from contradictions.
approach: BRIDGE performs triangular fixed-point refinement to explicitly couple Observable, Latent, and Memory states before decoding, with theoretical guarantees of convergence to a unique fixed point ensuring internal consistency.
contribution: Achieves highest scores on PersonaGym (4.59 avg.) and CoSER (59.5% avg.), with 8.0 point gain on Character Fidelity over baselines while updating only 0.85% of parameters.

problem: Existing synthetic datasets are insufficient for robust bimanual manipulation due to lack of self-correcting mechanisms for execution failures and scarcity of diverse visual and spatial variations for sim-to-real transfer.
approach: RoboTwin 2.0 integrates MLLMs with simulation-in-the-loop verification to automatically resolve task execution failures, and incorporates structured domain randomization across five axes (clutter, lighting, background, height, language) for diverse data generation.
contribution: Vision-Language-Action models pre-trained on synthetic data achieve 3.6× improvement in few-shot real-world transfer and 2.2× gain in zero-shot generalization across 50 dual-arm tasks.

problem: Existing adversarial robustness defenses lack formal guarantees, depend on restrictive assumptions, offer only point-wise certification, and overlook the inherent stochasticity of modern training pipelines.
approach: Views gradient-based training as a discrete-time stochastic dynamical system and uses barrier certificates to derive sufficient conditions for probabilistically certifying robust radius against worst-case poisoning attacks.
contribution: Provides formally guaranteed robustness against ℓp-bounded poisoning through probably approximately correct (PAC) guarantees, verified on MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR-10.

problem: It remains unclear how much model capacity is necessary to support implicit reasoning (inferring new facts from learned knowledge without explicit chain-of-thought) during pretraining.
approach: Pretrains language models from scratch in a controlled synthetic environment mimicking knowledge graphs, evaluating multi-hop inference ability and deriving a scaling law linking optimal parameter budget to graph search entropy.
contribution: Shows optimally sized models can reliably reason over approximately 0.008 bits of information per parameter, characterizing minimal sufficient capacity for implicit reasoning.

problem: Semi-supervised learning with only small proportion of labeled target samples typically requires transfer from semantically meaningful source domains, yet existing work overlooks synthetic noise domains as surrogates.
approach: Formulates Semi-Supervised Noise Adaptation (SSNA) which leverages synthetic noise domains to improve target generalization, proposing Noise Adaptation Framework (NAF) that establishes a generalization bound characterizing noise domain effects.
contribution: Demonstrates NAF effectively leverages noise domains to tighten generalization bounds and improve target domain performance in semi-supervised settings.

problem: Test-time adaptation offers compelling remedies for domain shift but conventional evaluations ignore accuracy-latency trade-offs, overlooking temporal pressure that constrains viability in latency-sensitive deployments.
approach: Introduces Tempora framework with temporal scenarios modeling deployment constraints, evaluation protocols, and time-contingent utility metrics quantifying accuracy-latency trade-offs through discrete, continuous, and amortised utilities.
contribution: Reveals rank instability across 750+ temporal evaluations spanning diverse datasets and hardware, showing no single TTA method dominates under all temporal constraints.

problem: Dynamic Sparse Training suffers from optimization instability in LLM training, manifested as loss spikes after topology updates due to cold-start issues for newly regrown parameters.
approach: Proposes Sparse Memory-Efficient Training (SMET) which stabilizes DST with optimizer warm-up for newly regrown parameters and density-aware learning-rate scaling, storing gradients and states only for active parameters.
contribution: Enables stable, scalable, and memory-efficient sparse pre-training of LLMs, providing theoretical analysis of update behaviors and demonstrating practical scalability.

problem: Invariant learning can fail to recover spurious correlation when the invariant structure is statistically identifiable, suggesting conditional computational barriers prevent polynomial-time learning.
approach: Shows under black-box sparse recovery assumptions that samplable multi-environment instances exist with learnable invariant subspace by exhaustive search but cannot be solved by polynomial-time algorithms.
contribution: Quantifies environment diversity effect on identifiability and derives minimax risk scaling proportional to 1/γ² under label-induced shifts, with phase transition at n* ∝ k(d-k)/(|E|γ²).

problem: Catastrophic forgetting remains fundamental challenge when neural networks train sequentially on new tasks without access to prior task data.
approach: Reformulates continual learning as control problem where learning and preservation signals compete within neural activity dynamics, converting regularization penalties into preservation signals protecting prior-task representations.
contribution: Enables task discrimination and outperforms existing methods by recovering true prior-task curvature implicitly without explicit storage, achieving continual-natural gradient property.

problem: Spiking Neural Network conversion from ANNs uses traditional spike encoding schemes that severely underutilize available encoding space, leading to large accuracy degradation under low-timestep constraints.
approach: Proposes Temporal Weighted Encoding (TWE) which implicitly assigns exponentially decaying weights through recursive integration, with temporal and threshold relaxation to resolve weight pattern mismatches.
contribution: Achieves negligible conversion loss with significantly fewer timesteps, offering scalable and efficient solution for SNN deployment.

problem: Training data can be reconstructed from generative models through attacks, raising privacy and copyright concerns, with existing attacks requiring substantial computational resources and data access.
approach: Presents low-resource reconstruction attack targeting template-memorized images (TMI) where recurring layouts are memorized, operating through benign prompts and requiring minimal training set access.
contribution: Shows unintentional reconstruction is possible by naive users with simple prompts like 'blue Unisex T-Shirt', revealing novel TMI phenomena and questions about generated content novelty.

problem: Supervised fine-tuning of vision-language models is vulnerable to backdoor attacks where poisoned responses are inserted, with existing defenses ineffective in open-ended generation settings.
approach: Proposes BYORn, identifying semantically implausible poisoned responses and dynamically replacing them with model-generated alternatives, with objective gradient corresponding to empirical risk upper bound over clean data.
contribution: Consistently improves robustness to backdoor attacks while preserving clean-task performance, remaining effective against adaptive attacks designed to circumvent the defense.

problem: Existing 3D environment generation methods cannot produce worlds that simultaneously are navigable over long-range spatial extents and cover complete omnidirectional field of view (360° horizontal, 180° vertical).
approach: SphericalDreamer generates multiple panoramic images and lifts them into 3D while maintaining visual and geometric consistency, enabling generation of fully immersive long-range 3D outdoor environments from text prompts.
contribution: Produces highly detailed, fully immersive 3D environments while substantially improving scale and navigability compared to prior approaches.

problem: Video object removal methods using diffusion models rely on noise-to-data paradigm, discarding rich structural priors from input video, leading to incomplete erasure and implausible filled content.
approach: Reformulates video object removal as video-to-video translation via stochastic bridge model, establishing direct stochastic path from source video to target, with adaptive mask modulation strategy balancing fidelity and generative flexibility.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods in visual quality and temporal consistency by leveraging input video as strong structural prior.

problem: Federated learning with bandwidth-constrained clients and fixed small sub-models leads to underdimensionality in later rounds, causing slow convergence and poor generalization.
approach: Proposes FedGMR with Gradual Model Restoration (GMR) that progressively increases sub-model density during training via mask-aware aggregation and asynchronous coordination.
contribution: Shows aggregation error scales with average sub-model density, with FedGMR improving convergence speed and final accuracy, especially under severe heterogeneity and non-IID distributions.

problem: Current LLMs often generate plausible-looking but ineffective research ideas; it is unclear whether automated execution feedback enables LLMs to learn and discover novel methods.
approach: Builds automated executor to implement ideas and launch parallel GPU experiments, converting LLM pre-training and post-training into execution environments with evolutionary search and reinforcement learning on feedback.
contribution: Execution-guided evolutionary search outperforms GRPO baseline on post-training and nanoGPT baseline on pre-training within ten search epochs, though RL suffers from mode collapse.

problem: Autoregressive image generation must decode long sequences of visual tokens with memory and latency bottlenecked by self-attention KV cache, while KV compression for AR visual generation remains underexplored.
approach: Introduces SparseAR, entropy-aware sparse attention method that identifies information-rich regions via entropy and adaptively adjusts attention sparsity, dynamically reducing KV-cache overhead during decoding.
contribution: Significantly improves inference efficiency while maintaining or improving generation and editing quality across four representative AR models on multiple benchmarks.

problem: Learning motion latents for robotic manipulation from visual sequences requires effective action abstractions that depend on understanding three-dimensional geometric transformations, not just visual patterns.
approach: GeoMoLa learns discrete motion latent codes by predicting point cloud evolution during manipulation rather than reconstructing visual observations, using four-dimensional (spatial geometry through time) objective.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art using only single-view RGB-D input, with learned codes exhibiting effective motion abstraction and robust manipulation in cluttered real-world environments.

problem: Vision-language models remain brittle under real-world corruptions, where parameter-efficient adaptation through Euclidean alignment is not semantics-preserving and can harm downstream reasoning.
approach: Proposes Manifold-Adversarial Adapters (MAA), parameter-efficient layer-wise modules that steer corrupted features back onto clean in-distribution manifold via paired feature self-distillation and token-level adversarial constraint.
contribution: Consistently improves performance over baselines, enabling single-stage robustness with negligible overhead without latency or semantic drift of restoration pipelines.

problem: Multimodal image fusion suffers from cross-modal discrepancies and local conflicts creating uncertain modality allocation, causing information loss or artifact propagation.
approach: Formulates fusion as observation-conditioned probabilistic decision-learning problem using cross-modal differences as decision triggers, constructing spatial and spectral decision conditions mapped to interpretable contribution policies.
contribution: Demonstrates stable and competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods on multiple fusion tasks with uncertainty modulation for conservative mixing under insufficient evidence.

problem: Large language models demonstrate strong semantic reasoning but their quantitative reasoning remains unreliable despite recent progress in tool-augmented inference.
approach: Decouples reasoning from computation by assigning LLMs to planning and analysis while delegating numerical computation to specialized tools constructed during planning, with iterative refinement through self-play in digital twin markets.
contribution: Enhances quantitative reliability of LLM-driven decision-making through bounded self-evolving loop, coupling high-level planning with robust quantitative execution.

problem: Masked diffusion language models decode by iteratively unmasking tokens where unmasking order (order of thought) strongly influences generation quality but is typically chosen heuristically.
approach: Derives tractable upper bound on sequential decoding mismatch via KL divergence and pathwise log-likelihood, casting order selection as principled policy optimization with frozen denoiser via Group Relative Policy Optimization.
contribution: Self-Aware Scheduling (SAS) improves Sudoku accuracy from 82.0% to 91.8% on 1B MDM and GSM8K pass@1 from 64% to 76%, consistently matching or exceeding heuristic schedules.

problem: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) makes explicit link with specific human choice normative model, but its full generality and normative framework connections remain unexplored.
approach: Elevates DPO's connection to full generality of preference optimization normative framework, reworking social choice theory for ML fit and revealing support for non-convex losses and broad embedding of any ML analytical choice with any human choice model.
contribution: Unveils unexpected riches for ML including non-convex loss support and framework umbrella wide enough to safeguard DPO extensions (margins, length correction).

problem: LLM-powered multi-agent systems enable communication but create attack surface where malicious agents propagate misinformation; embedding-based defenses fail when attacker messages are close to benign ones.
approach: Proposes using confidence scores (logits) to prune or down-weight messages during MAS communication, leveraging token-level signals when embeddings are not distinguishable under attack.
contribution: Shows improved robustness across models and datasets, revealing effectiveness of confidence signals decays over communication rounds, highlighting importance of early intervention.

problem: Understanding complex brain interactions requires capturing higher-order dependencies across multiple regions, but existing graph-based methods focus on pairwise interactions and predefined hyperedges limit flexibility.
approach: Introduces MuHL, adaptive multi-scale hyperedge learning framework that constructs hierarchical node features and dynamically learns high-order interactions through continuous hyperedge construction over multi-resolution signals.
contribution: Consistently improves disease classification across different stages on multiple brain network benchmarks, identifying key ROIs and group-wise interactions associated with disease progression.

problem: Episodic MDPs with heavy-tailed losses lack Best-of-Both-Worlds algorithms balancing instance-independent regret in adversarial environments and logarithmic instance-dependent regret in stochastic settings.
approach: Proposes HT-FTRL-OM and HT-FTRL-UOB applying Follow-The-Regularized-Leader framework over occupancy measures with novel skipping loss estimators, achieving polynomial regret bounds under heavy-tailed losses.
contribution: Achieves Õ(T^1/α) regret in adversarial regimes and O(log T) regret in stochastic regimes for known transitions, with extension to unknown transitions.

problem: Hierarchical decision-making frameworks struggle to balance RL's difficulty with constraint satisfaction and OC's myopic and computationally prohibitive formulations in hierarchical RL-OC architectures.
approach: Proposes principled inverse optimization framework that informs lower-level problem structure from expert demonstrations, ensuring lower-level policy remains aligned with overall long-term task goal.
contribution: Consistently outperforms strong baselines in efficiency and decision quality on network resource allocation and continuous collision avoidance tasks.

problem: Standard Direct Preference Optimization treats all preference pairs uniformly, overlooking heterogeneous learning demands where semantic understanding and preference discrimination require different learning paces.
approach: Proposes Gradient-Guided Disentangled DPO (GDO-DPO) with curriculum framework that independently regulates learning pace per layer based on gradient stability, addressing layer-wise localization of semantic complexity and preference uncertainty.
contribution: Improves over DPO by 4.1% on AlpacaEval 2.0 with particularly strong gains on reasoning-intensive tasks.

problem: Mirror descent under classic smoothness assumption fails for non-smooth objectives with Lipschitz gradient constants growing with gradient norm, restricting applicability in modern ML.
approach: Introduces ℓ*-smoothness concept measuring Hessian norms in terms of general norm and dual, establishing convergence for mirror-descent algorithms with generalized self-bounding property for gradient control.
contribution: Establishes sharp convergence rates for deterministic, stochastic, non-convex and composite optimization, matching state-of-the-art under classic smoothness.

problem: Capturing local variations in long time series is challenging especially in medical signals where local variations indicate pathological events, with traditional global-local branches learning similar representations.
approach: Proposes Dual-Stream Enhancement Mechanism that structurally enlarges differences between global and local patterns, reducing feature coupling and enabling weak interactions.
contribution: DSENet achieves state-of-the-art performance on blood glucose prediction with extremely low computational cost, demonstrating strong application potential.

problem: Discrete visual generation methods struggle with performance gaps versus continuous methods, suffering degradation or prohibitive training costs when scaling codebook size.
approach: Proposes Masked Bit Autoregressive modeling (BAR), scalable framework supporting arbitrary codebook sizes, where autoregressive transformer predicts tokens by progressively generating constituent bits.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art gFID of 0.99 on ImageNet-256, significantly reducing sampling costs and converging faster than continuous approaches.

problem: Scientific problem solving requires both deep domain knowledge and complex reasoning, yet lacks widely adopted holistic benchmark and systematic disentanglement of knowledge versus reasoning roles.
approach: Introduces SciReas benchmark suite and KRUX probing framework to study distinct roles of reasoning and knowledge, finding retrieval of task-relevant knowledge from model parameters is critical bottleneck.
contribution: Demonstrates reasoning models consistently benefit from external knowledge in-context, and enhanced verbalized reasoning improves ability to surface task-relevant knowledge.

problem: Web GUI agent training relies on expensive and difficult to verify interaction trajectories from real websites, with hidden state transitions requiring inconsistent external verifiers.
approach: Proposes AutoWebWorld synthesizing controllable verifiable web environments as Finite State Machines, with coding agents translating FSMs into interactive websites enabling programmatic verification.
contribution: Generates over 11,663 verified trajectories from 29 environments at $0.04 per trajectory, with 7B agent achieving state-of-the-art on WebVoyager, showing clear scaling law with synthetic data volume.

problem: Inferring protein levels from RNA data faces geometric bottleneck where enforcing deterministic constraints on noisy heteroscedastic data collapses intrinsic uncertainty, destabilizing learning.
approach: Presents scChord, noise-decoupled conditional flow matching framework using probabilistic decoder to disentangle technical noise and over-dispersion from raw counts, enabling rectified latent manifold.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art inference accuracy while faithfully reconstructing high-fidelity biological heterogeneity and complex protein distributions.

problem: Plug-and-Play diffusion prior solvers function as memoryless operators, updating estimates solely on instantaneous gradients, leading to non-vanishing steady-state bias under heavy corruption.
approach: Proposes Dual-Coupled PnP Diffusion (DC-PnPDP) restoring dual variable for integral feedback, with Spectral Homogenization mechanism modulating structured artifacts into pseudo-AWGN inputs.
contribution: Resolves bias-hallucination trade-off achieving state-of-the-art fidelity with significantly accelerated convergence on CT and MRI reconstruction.

problem: LLMs have absorbed malicious scam content into weights and reproduce it during inference with low-resource attacks requiring no jailbreaking, exemplified by ChatGPT generating phishing URLs in code.
approach: Introduces Scam2Prompt automated auditing framework crawling scam websites, inferring intent, and synthesizing innocuous developer-style prompts to evaluate if LLMs reproduce scam endpoints.
contribution: Evaluates seven production LLMs showing vulnerability is persistent with malicious code generation rates from 12.9% to 47.3%, with guardrails offering limited protection.
